title: History of the Boston Marathon (BAA)
claims: The Boston Athletic Association was established in 1887.

The first Boston Marathon was run on 19 April 1897; John J. McDermott of New York won from a 15-member starting field in 2:55:10, from Metcalf's Mill in Ashland to the Irvington Oval near Copley Square.

Roberta Gibb was the first woman to run the Boston Marathon in 1966, finishing in 3:21:40; Kathrine Switzer was the first woman to complete with a bib number in 1967; the women's division was officially established in 1972.
The Boston Marathon officially recognized a wheelchair division in 1975 with Bob Hall, who finished in two hours 58 minutes.
The 124th Boston Marathon (2020) was postponed from April and held as a fully virtual event with a September 5-14 completion window; the 125th (2021) was the first fall edition of the race.
